findings.summary: REVIEW-JOURNAL-01 at 62ab30a changes exactly the three allowed app paths plus the report. It turns the review namespace marker into an authenticated v2 body that binds format, namespace, resolved path, and directory, log and marker identities, using bigint dev/ino stored as decimal strings. The marker is checked before the delegate opens, again before and after every operation, and on close; any v1 store is quarantined unchanged, the review key derivation is byte-identical, and no cost grammar, API change or live v1 reader was added. Every spec criterion has real evidence: 39 new tests on the real reviewFixture and journal, the actual controller run (257 pass, 3 explicit skips, 0 fail), build, the 04-C checker and diagnostics, all four probes (the root marker probe was red on a18d82e and is green here), and four current native scenarios. The Windows in-process directory trigger and the two symlink cases are disclosed as skipped, not passed, and I confirmed the trigger-to-latch path by reading the code. My remaining findings are minor or nit only; full 05-A/05-B/05-G and every real-world gate stay open.

findings.title: Windows directory trigger unexercised; latch path confirmed by reading only
findings.problem: On Windows the OS refused to rename the open journal directory (EPERM), so the in-process directory-mismatch test was skipped. Before skipping, it showed the identity, disk bytes, primary rows and a real read were all unchanged. I read the file through EOF and confirmed the path that test would have exercised. verify() (170-177) calls readMarker() before and after the delegate's full-chain records('operator'). readMarker calls paths() (100-105) at its start and again at its end (133). paths() runs checkDirectory (83-86) and then inspectLog (87-99), which itself checks the directory before and after the log descriptor/path comparison. A missing path seen during a swap is turned into recovery_quarantined by observed() (29-34). checked() (178-190) runs verify before and after each operation, sets broken=true on recovery_quarantined (186), and rejects every later call (179, 183). Nothing resets broken (it is only set false at 79), and close() (204-217) releases resources without clearing it. Live marker/log replacement exercises the same latch and passed, and closed-store directory substitution and relocation passed for both empty and populated stores. This is code-reading evidence only, not an executed Windows result.
findings.fix_check: The planning receipt says verbatim that the app-side directory-trigger branch is SKIPPED on Windows (OS denied the rename) and that its latch path was confirmed by reading the code only. The two symlink cases stay listed as EPERM skips. No receipt or merge text calls these exercised or passed.

findings.title: One malformed record blocks the journal instance for every household
findings.problem: checked() sets the sticky broken flag on any recovery_quarantined from work(), not only from the store verification. The queue delegate's fact()/append() decode errors include per-input problems, for example a tampered review_slice_commands.sealed_fact. review-service decoded() and finish() pass primary rows to fact() and append(). One bad row in household A now makes every later journal call for every household fail with 503 until a new instance is opened. In baseline a18d82e, only A's history failed. This fails closed and matches the accepted cost-journal pattern (cost-journal.mjs:158). However, the spec says 'no ... review semantics change', and the hardening doc does not describe this cross-household availability coupling.
findings.fix_check: The receipt or doc states that a single quarantined fact/append input latches the whole instance until it is reopened. Alternatively, a later authorized revision latches only on verify() or delegate store-integrity failures and adds a test showing a bad primary row in one household leaves another household's reads working.

findings.title: Full log re-verified twice per operation; reads scale with rows × log
findings.problem: verify() reloads, MAC-checks and decrypts every frame through delegate.records('operator'), plus about four marker reads and directory-ancestor walks, both before and after each call. That includes fact(), which review-service history() calls for every row (up to 1000), and construction runs history for every household. Each read therefore costs about 2 × rows × the full 16 MB-bounded log. That is acceptable for disposable synthetic stores and matches the cost-journal precedent, but it is not disclosed as a scalability or availability limit.
findings.fix_check: The receipt and carried limits note per-operation full-chain re-verification as a known local-only cost. No capacity or production claim depends on it.

findings.title: App docs carry a wrong short hash and no final executed counts
findings.problem: Both controller checkpoints (doc line 53, REPORT line 55) cite setup-r4 source '3532ec70'. That is not a prefix of the actual 3532ec7fa481570edf9314985cb602bcd6ec851a; the eighth character differs ('0' vs 'f'). The controller disclosed this erratum. Setup-r4's first finding also asked the doc and REPORT to state the final-source counts. They state only the 39-case and 2-case attempt counts and point to external evidence (257 pass, 3 skip, 0 fail out of 260 at 62ab30a). Runtime and gates are unaffected, but merged provenance text stays inaccurate.
findings.fix_check: The planning partial receipt records the full setup-r4 commit and the exact-source 260/257/3/0 counts, and says the app text still contains the typo. Any later authorized app-doc revision corrects it.

findings.title: 'wrong-identity-authenticated' fails on format, not the identity binding
findings.problem: marker_identity '0001:0002' has leading zeros, so it is rejected by the persistedIdentity format check (review-journal.mjs:24) before the identity comparison (line 125) runs. The binding is still proven by the copy tests, where a correctly MAC'd marker sits on a different inode, but this case's name suggests more than it tests.
findings.fix_check: In a later authorized test revision, sign a well-formed but different identity (for example '1:2') so the rejection comes from the binding comparison.

findings.title: Second assertion in the genuine-v1 test always passes
findings.problem: assert.deepEqual(bytes, signed(keys, oldBody)) compares a deterministic HMAC with itself, so it proves nothing. The test still meets the criterion: signed() uses the real 'review-local-01\0namespace-marker\0' derivation over canonical({format:'review-journal-v1',namespace_verifier}), which matches the baseline markerMAC shown in the diff's removed lines. It also checks the exact v1 field set and that the bytes are not rewritten.
findings.fix_check: No action needed. Optionally remove the self-comparison or replace it with a check against a fixed baseline vector.

findings.title: Reviewer coverage and limits for feature-r1
findings.problem: I read these in full through EOF this round. Authority: SOURCE_OF_TRUTH, AGENTS, GOVERNANCE, approved/APPROVALS, PROJECT_CONTEXT v1.101 lines 1-1366, the four engineering-v1 files (README, ENGINEERING_DESIGN_V1 lines 1-410, MODULE_GUIDE, REVIEW_NOTES), both standing APPROVAL-012/013 records, the CODEX-05-B card and the approved SYNTHETIC_REVIEW_LIFECYCLE_SLICE. Prior slice: the REVIEW-LOCAL-01 grant, REVIEW_LOCAL_SLICE_SPEC and the slice-result JSON. Setup: the frozen spec, the REVIEW-JOURNAL-01 grant, review_journal_slice.py, test_review_journal_slice.py, review_journal_probe.mjs, setup-r2 and r4 in full, and setup-r1 and r3 findings and summaries (lines 1-48 and 1-32, without their controller_checks tails). App originals: review-service, review-page, lib/loop/review-client, queue-journal, continuation-journal, cost-journal, loop-review-service.test, loop-review-ui.test, loop-cost-service.test, loop-cost-ui.test, and the generationFixture key setup. New app files: server/review-journal.mjs and tests/loop-review-marker.test.mjs from disk through EOF. The hardening doc and REPORT I read fully from the supplied diff and spot-checked on disk (lines 49-55). Limits: I ran nothing; check and native results are as the controller supplied them. I could not use git, so I recomputed no blob or SHA-256. I reconstructed the baseline a18d82e review-journal from the diff's removed and context lines plus the unchanged lines. I did not read REVIEW-LOCAL-01-SETUP4.json, REVIEW_LOCAL_FOURTH_SETUP_REVIEW.md, the generation, review or cost probe sources, check_application_card.py, or the native screenshots.
findings.fix_check: No action. A later round rereads any original that changes.
